themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 500% increase (z-score: 5.0)—suggesting either coordinated tree vandalism or a single major incident affecting the canopy.
evidence: 3 complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Pattern emerged last week with 3 complaints, sustaining this week
Illegal tree damage is rare baseline issue, making spike statistically significant
reporting_angles: Canvass blocks where complaints clustered to identify if single incident (storm, construction) or pattern of intentional damage
Interview Parks Department about enforcement response and whether crews have noticed coordinated damage

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees/Branches Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 10 complaints THIS WEEK versus 3.0 weekly average—a 233% increase (z-score: 3.74)—indicating possible deferred tree maintenance or seasonal growth outpacing city response.
evidence: 10 complaints this week vs. 3.0 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 3.74)
Spike emerged this week, not sustained from prior weeks
Converges with illegal tree damage spike, suggesting broader tree management issue
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department tree maintenance schedule for CD 317—are crews understaffed or behind on pruning?
Map complaint locations to see if issue is localized to specific blocks or citywide pattern

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Alert
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)—the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset, warranting immediate investigation into potential contamination or perception crisis.
evidence: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest z-score in dataset)
Water quality is typically rare complaint, making spike extraordinary
No follow-up complaints in last 2 weeks, suggesting either resolved or unreported
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP water quality test results for East Flatbush from 3 weeks ago; cross-reference with complaints to identify affected blocks
Interview residents who filed complaints to determine if issue was discoloration, odor, taste, or health symptom—and whether it persists

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker/vehicle complaints surged to 4 complaints last week versus 0.6 weekly average—a 540% increase (z-score: 3.94)—coupled with dumpster complaints up 700% 2 weeks ago (5 vs. 0.6 avg), suggesting systemic collection or worker conduct issues.
evidence: Sanitation worker complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 3.94)
Dumpster complaints: 5 two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.29)
Two separate but related complaint types spiking in same 2-week window suggests operational failure
reporting_angles: Request DSNY route manifests and supervisor logs for CD 317 to identify if specific crew or truck reassignment occurred 2-3 weeks ago
Interview 311 callers about nature of complaints: missed pickups, overflowing bins, worker conduct, or vehicle damage?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Disorder
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 5 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 1.0 weekly average—a 400% increase (z-score: 4.0)—suggesting possible surge in Uber/Lyft activity or illegal street-hailing in East Flatbush.
evidence: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (400% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago but no follow-up data available for past week
Complaint type is historically low-volume, making increase significant
reporting_angles: Query TLC data for vehicle activity changes in CD 317 over past month—new bases, increased pickups near transit hubs, hotspot violations?
Determine if complaints centered on specific location (e.g., near subway station, commercial corridor) suggesting localized problem
